summary.text: The task is to judge the exact BOOK ENTRY against the strongest specific alternative using the scriptural evidence.

  "persuasion": "PERSUADED",
  "support_scope": "FULL",
  "rationale": "The printed entry’s core—that storm/tempest figures the nations in turmoil as the raging sea, stilled by Christ’s word—is the best-supported reading of the four supplied texts taken together. Ps 65:7 and Isa 17:12-13 place seas/waves and whirlwind in explicit parallel with the tumult/rushing of peoples and nations; Luke 21:25 repeats the same parallel (“distress of nations\u2026 the sea and the waves roaring”); Mark 4:39 then shows Jesus employing the identical stilling language. No rival reading accounts for this four-text chain with equal economy or fewer unsupported steps. Common alternatives (personal trials, generic theophany, chaoskampf) either ignore the nation-sea glosses or treat them as ornamental, leaving the cross-references unexplained.",
  "book_core_identification": "Storm/tempest = the nations in turmoil (the raging sea), stilled at Christ’s word “Peace, be still.”",
  "book_secondary_elaborations": [
    "Identification of the raging sea with the nations in turmoil",
    "Christ’s word of stilling (“Peace, be still”) as the act that quiets that turmoil"
  ],
  "unsupported_glossary_assertions": [],
  "chapter_only_objections": [
    "Broader claim that virtually every sea/waters occurrence = peoples (including floods as armies, fish as men, islands as set-apart peoples, “no more sea” as end of restless humanity)",
    "Typological extensions to Red Sea, Babylon, Tyre, molten sea, sea of glass, living water contrast, etc.",
    "Methodological assertions about parallel columns, next-verse rule, and personification flags as universal decoding keys"
  ],
  "strongest_counter_interpretation": "Storm/tempest primarily symbolizes either (a) the believer’s personal trials and adversities that Christ calms or (b) divine judgment/theophany/power over primordial chaos, with the nation-sea language treated as poetic ornament rather than definitional.",
  "counter_core_identification": "Storm = personal trials of faith or God’s judgmental/theophanic power over nature/chaos",
  "counter_relation_to_book_core": "CONTRADICTS",
  "material_core_denial": "The counter denies that the primary and consistent referent of the storm/raging sea in the cited texts is the nations in turmoil, treating that equation as secondary metaphor or devotional application rather than the symbol’s established meaning.",
  "counter_case": [
    "Mark 4:35-41 (and parallels) is the dominant pastoral text and is almost universally applied to “storms of life.”",
    "Many OT storm texts (Nahum 1:3, Job 38:1, Jeremiah 23:19, etc.) function as theophany or wrath without an explicit nation-sea gloss.",
    "Chaoskampf background and power-over-nature readings explain Jesus’ authority without requiring a peoples-symbol.",
    "Luke 21:25 can be read as literal cosmic signs plus general distress, not a definitional parallel."
  ],
  "book_explanatory_advantages": [
    "Ps 65:7 and Isa 17:12-13 supply inspired parallel columns that equate seas/waves/whirlwind with tumult of peoples/nations; Luke 21:25 repeats the identical construction.",
    "Mark 4:39 uses the same stilling vocabulary already defined in Ps 65:7, so the miracle signs dominion over the nations rather than merely weather or private affliction.",
    "The four cited texts form a closed, mutually reinforcing set that needs no external chaos or trial framework.",
    "Isa 17:13’s whirlwind chasing nations supplies the tempest half of the entry without remainder."
  ],
  "counter_explanatory_advantages": [
    "Matches the overwhelming majority of popular and homiletic usage of the stilling miracle.",

support_scope.description: Support for the exact glossary BOOK ENTRY only, never for the supporting chapter as a whole.

book_secondary_elaborations.description: Secondary assertions actually printed in the glossary BOOK ENTRY; exclude chapter-only claims.

unsupported_glossary_assertions.description: Material assertions actually printed in the BOOK ENTRY that the evidence does not support. Must be empty for FULL and nonempty for CORE_ONLY.

chapter_only_objections.description: Objections to applications or arguments found only in the supporting chapter. Preserved for later chapter review and excluded from the glossary scope ruling.

instructions: Return only the requested structured result. Judge the exact glossary entry against the strongest specific alternative; treat the chapter as evidence, not as an additional judgment target.
